title: Arriving in Africa: flights, airports and transfers
excerpt: Which airport to fly into for each of our safaris, how transfers work, and the documents to sort out before you go.

body.p: Our safari prices cover your accommodation and transfers on the ground, while international flights are booked separately, either by you or by us on request. Here is where you'll be flying to, and what happens when you land.

ul: Cape Town International, for Cape Town, the Winelands and the Garden Route
Johannesburg O.R. Tambo, for Kruger, the Panorama Route, Sun City and Pilanesberg, and many regional connections
Victoria Falls International, for Victoria Falls and Hwange
Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta, for the Masai Mara
Kilimanjaro International, for the Serengeti and Ngorongoro Crater
Zanzibar Abeid Amani Karume, for Zanzibar's beaches

body.p: We arrange every transfer on your itinerary, starting with a meet-and-greet at the airport. Your driver will be waiting in arrivals with a name board, and will take you to your hotel or lodge. Flights between safari areas are often on small aircraft to bush airstrips, with luggage limits. We'll confirm the allowance for your route.

ul: Passport validity and blank pages: requirements differ by country, so check well ahead
Visas: these depend on your nationality and every country on your route
Health requirements, including any vaccination certificates
Comprehensive travel insurance covering your whole trip

body.p: Entry rules can change, so always confirm requirements with the relevant embassy or official government website before you travel. We'll point you in the right direction for your route.

Book international flights once your safari dates are confirmed, and allow time between connections, especially if you are flying on to a bush airstrip on the same day. If you'd like us to look at flight options for you, just ask when you enquire.
